q: 1. In brick masonry, for good bonding
options: all bricks need not be uniform in size
bats must be used in alternate courses only
vertical joints in alternate courses should fall in plumb
cement mortar used must have surkhi as additive
explain: Strong bonding requires that vertical joints do not align across consecutive courses. Having vertical joints 'fall in plumb' (aligning every other course) ensures maximum load distribution.

q: 2. Expansion joints in masonry walls are provided if length exceeds
explain: To prevent cracking due to thermal expansion and contraction, long masonry walls must have expansion joints at intervals, typically capped at a maximum of 40 meters.

q: 3. The nominal thickness of the brick wall in mm, is
explain: While a standard modular brick is 190mm long, the 'nominal' thickness includes the mortar joint, bringing the standard wall thickness calculation to 200mm.

q: 4. The arrangement made to support an unsafe structure temporarily, is known as
explain: Shoring is the process of temporarily supporting a building, vessel, structure, or trench with shores (props) when in danger of collapse or during alterations.

q: 5. The overlapping of bricks or stones in masonry is called ...........
explain: Bonding is the arrangement of bricks or stones to ensure they overlap, preventing continuous vertical joints and distributing loads throughout the wall.

q: 6. Numbers of bricks required for one cubic meter masonry wall as per Nepal standard
explain: Standard practice in Nepal estimates approximately 560 bricks per cubic meter for traditional brick masonry including mortar joints.

q: 7. A brick or stone put in position in the masonry such that its length is perpendicular to the face of the wall is known as ...........
explain: A header is a brick laid so that only its smallest face (end) is visible on the surface of the wall.

q: 8. In Nepal, the generally used method of bond in masonry wall of brickwork is
explain: English bond is widely preferred for its superior strength, consisting of alternate courses of headers and stretchers.

q: 9. Stretcher bond is possible only in ...........
explain: Since stretcher bond only shows the long face of the brick, it can only be used for walls that are half-a-brick thick (partition walls).

q: 10. The stretcher bond in brick masonry can be used only when the wall is of
explain: Stretcher bond lacks internal ties across the wall thickness, making it suitable only for partition walls (half-brick thick).

q: 11. Which of the following is not a tool used in laying brick wall
explain: An auger is a drilling tool used for soil or wood; it is not used in bricklaying like a trowel or plumb bob.

q: 12. A bond in which stretcher bricks are laid on edge in alternate courses forming continuous cavity is known as ..........
explain: Soldier bond involves bricks laid vertically on their ends (on edge), often used for decorative purposes or window sills.

q: 13. A load bearing partition wall is called ..........
explain: While many partitions are non-load-bearing, if an internal wall carries structural weight, it is referred to as an internal load-bearing wall.

q: 14. Brick masonry constructed within a framework of wooden member to act as a partition wall is called ..........
explain: Brick nogging is a type of wall construction where bricks are used to fill the spaces between timber studs in a wood frame.

q: 15. The member laid horizontally to support common rafters and which transmits the loads to the trusses or wall are
explain: Purlins are horizontal beams that run parallel to the ridge to support the common rafters.

q: 16. The minimum thickness of a wall in stone masonry cannot be less than
explain: Because stone units are large and irregular, stone masonry walls must have a minimum thickness (usually 35-40 cm) to ensure stability.

q: 17. The inclined surface on the abutment which acts as a seat for the arch is known as ..........
explain: The skewback is the sloped surface on the abutment from which the arch units start their curve.

q: 18. For a building one side of the busy street where the ordinary scaffolding will obstruct the traffic on the road, the type of scaffolding provided is
explain: Needle scaffolding (cantilever scaffolding) is supported by 'needles' passing through the wall, keeping the ground level clear for traffic.

q: 19. An arch which is formed by two arcs of circles meeting at the apex point is known as ..........
explain: Pointed arches consist of two intersecting curves, typical in Gothic architecture.

q: 20. In a pointed arch if the apex point and the springing points become corners of an isosceles triangle, then it is known as ..........
explain: A lancet arch is a narrow, tall pointed arch where the height is much greater than the width.

q: 21. If after every three or four stretchers, one header is used in a brick masonry wall, then the bond so formed will be called as
explain: English Garden Wall bond consists of several courses of stretchers followed by one course of headers (typically 3:1 or 5:1 ratio).

q: 22. The most important tool used by a mason in laying of bricks while constructing a wall is
explain: The trowel is the primary tool for lifting, spreading, and leveling mortar, as well as for 'tapping' bricks into their correct position.

q: 23. When rise of an arch is more than half of span of the arch and its lower portion is straight instead of circular, then it is called as
explain: A stilted arch has vertical 'stilts' below the curve, making the total height greater than half the span.

q: 24. When rise of an arch is more than the span, then the arch is called as
explain: Lancet arches are very tall and narrow pointed arches, where the rise significantly exceeds the span.

q: 25. In any case of the bearing of a lintel should not be less than
explain: The minimum structural bearing (overlap) for a lintel onto a wall is standardly 10 cm to ensure load distribution.

q: 26. Air conditioning means ..........
options: cooling, purifying and controlling humidity of air
explain: Air conditioning involves complete 'treatment' of air, including temperature control, humidity control, and filtration.

q: 27. For the construction of 10 cm thick brick wall, the bond preferred is ..........
explain: A 10 cm (half-brick) wall is built by laying bricks end-to-end, known as a stretcher bond.

q: 28. The total horizontal force P per meter length of a retaining wall of height H holding a soil of density Y and angle of internal friction φ is given by ........
options: P = yH * (1 - sin φ)/(1 + sin φ)
P = yH * (1 + sin φ)/(1 - sin φ)
explain: Based on Rankine's Theory, the total pressure is (1/2) * γ * H² * Ka, where Ka = (1 - sin φ)/(1 + sin φ).

q: 29. The cavity wall is generally provided for ..........
explain: The air gap in a cavity wall acts as a barrier to moisture, heat transfer, and sound, significantly improving the building's internal environment.

q: 30. A brick which is half as wide as a full brick, is called ..........
explain: A queen closer is obtained by cutting a brick lengthwise into two equal halves.

q: 31. Cornice is defined as a ..........
options: horizontal course of masonry projecting from the face of the wall
horizontal moulded projection near the top of a building
covering placed on the exposed top of an external wall
triangular shaped portion of masonry at the end of a sloped roof
explain: A cornice is a decorative and functional horizontal projection that finishes the top of a wall or building.

q: 32. A bat is the portion of a ..........
options: brick cut in such a manner that its one long face remains uncut
explain: A brick bat is a piece of brick that has been cut across its width, usually classified as half-bat or three-quarter bat.

q: 33. The type of stone masonry commonly adopted in the construction of residential building is ..........
explain: Coursed rubble masonry is popular for residential work because it is stronger and more aesthetically pleasing than uncoursed types.

q: 34. Herring-bone bond is commonly used for ..........
explain: Herring-bone bond, where bricks are laid at 45 degrees, is highly decorative and provides excellent interlocking for floor pavings.

q: 35. A wall built to resist the pressure of earth filling, is known as ..........
explain: A retaining wall is a structural wall designed to hold back soil or other materials at a slope steeper than the natural angle of repose.

q: 36. A stone wall provided to protect the slopes of cutting in natural ground from the action of weather is known as ..........
explain: A breast wall is specifically designed to keep the natural ground slope in situ and protect it from weathering, unlike a retaining wall which usually supports backfill.

q: 37. In a brick nogging type of partition wall, the vertical wooden members are called ..........
explain: In timber framing or brick nogging, the vertical members are called 'studs' while the horizontal members are 'noggings'.

q: 38. The operation finishing mortar joints after completion of a masonry wall is called ..........
explain: Pointing is the process of raking out mortar joints to a depth of 13-20 mm and refilling them with superior mortar.

q: 39. In any case the bearing of a lintel should not be less than ..........
explain: Standard practice dictates a minimum bearing (overlap on the wall) of 15 cm or 1/10th to 1/12th of the span.

q: 40. For large spans the most suitable type of roof preferred is ..........
explain: Shell roofs are thin, curved R.C.C. structures that can cover very large spans without intermediate columns.

q: 41. The type of arch used for high class buildings where appearance is of prime importance, is known as ...........
explain: Gauged arches use bricks precisely cut to size and shape, allowing for very fine joints and a decorative look.

q: 42. A temporary structure to support an arch during construction is called ...........
explain: Centering is the temporary timber or steel framework that holds the bricks/stones of an arch in place until the mortar sets.
